title: Nvidia to release three new GeForce GTX graphics cards this month
summary: Nvidia plans to introduce three new GeForce GTX graphics cards later this month: the GeForce GTX 960, GeForce GTX 960 Ti, and GeForce GTX 965 Ti. These cards will target different market segments with varying performance levels, powered by GM206 and cut-down GM204 graphics processors. The success of the GTX 960 will largely depend on its pricing.

title: Nvidia details Tegra X1: 8 cores, 256 stream processors, 4K video and 20nm
summary: Nvidia introduced its latest Tegra X1 system-on-chip for mobile devices, featuring ARMv8 64-bit cores, Maxwell architecture graphics with 256 stream processors, and support for 4K video. The chip also handles up to six camera inputs with 100MP sensors, making it suitable for automotive applications. Manufactured using 20nm process technology, the Tegra X1 is a powerful mobile processor, although it lacks integrated broadband technology.

title: MSI sells 100 millionth Nvidia GeForce adapter, unveils limited edition graphics card
summary: MSI announced that it has sold over 100 million graphics cards based on Nvidia's GeForce processors and to celebrate, the company is releasing a special edition GeForce GTX 970 Gaming 100ME graphics card. This limited edition card will feature improved performance and a unique green color scheme. The article speculates on whether Nvidia will allow MSI to overclock the memory beyond typical limits for this special release.

title: The GTX 970/980 Maxwell GPUs Light Up With Nouveau On Linux 3.19
summary: This article details the initial support for NVIDIA's GeForce GTX 970 and GTX 980 Maxwell GPUs in the Linux 3.19 kernel via the open-source Nouveau DRM driver. While this initial support is limited to kernel mode-setting without hardware acceleration, due to pending NVIDIA firmware, testing confirmed successful mode-setting on Ubuntu 14.10. Full hardware acceleration and re-clocking capabilities are anticipated in future updates, despite current limitations.

title: Specs and performance of Nvidia GeForce GTX 960 revealed
summary: A Chinese website has reportedly leaked the specifications and preliminary benchmarks of Nvidia's upcoming GeForce GTX 960 graphics card. The new GPU, based on the GM206, is expected to offer performance comparable to the GeForce GTX 680 and GTX 770, potentially at a $200 price point, making it a competitive option despite its 128-bit memory controller. The article cautions that these are unofficial leaks and performance in 3DMark benchmarks may not accurately reflect real-world gaming.

title: Supermicro X10DRG-Q Review – GPU Compute Server Motherboard
summary: This article reviews the Supermicro X10DRG-Q, a GPU compute server motherboard designed for platforms requiring multiple PCIe accelerator cards like Tesla, Xeon Phi, or NVIDIA GPUs. The review details the motherboard's unique features, test configuration, thermal performance, and integrated management capabilities. The author concludes that the X10DRG-Q excels in accommodating high-powered PCIe expansion cards and is a top choice for quad Xeon Phi or Tesla/Quadro solutions.

title: iQIYI.com and NVIDIA Announce Establishment of the iQIYI-NVIDIA Research and Development Center
summary: iQIYI, a subsidiary of Baidu, and NVIDIA have announced a strategic partnership to establish the iQIYI-NVIDIA Research and Development Center. This collaboration aims to enhance iQIYI's deep learning and media cloud computing capabilities using NVIDIA's GPUs and deep learning architecture. The center will focus on improving iQIYI's video platform for a more personalized viewing experience for Chinese users, deploying technologies like machine learning, cloud rendering, cloud gaming, and virtual desktop infrastructure.

title: Nvidia vows to boost GeForce GTX 970 performance with driver update
summary: Nvidia has promised to address memory allocation issues and boost the performance of its GeForce GTX 970 graphics card through a new driver update. This comes after the company admitted to misrepresenting the card's specifications, including its memory architecture, actual memory bandwidth, and raster operations pipelines. While acknowledging the misstatement, Nvidia emphasizes that the GeForce GTX 970 still performs well in most scenarios.

title: Samsung to produce chips for Nvidia, Qualcomm – analyst
summary: An analyst predicts that Samsung will significantly improve its contract semiconductor manufacturing business by producing chips for Nvidia and Qualcomm starting in Q2 this year, leveraging its 14nm FinFET fabrication process. This move comes as chip designers seek to diversify FinFET chip suppliers due to concerns about yields and manufacturing capacities at TSMC, a long-time Nvidia supplier.

title: Supermicro X10DAX (Intel C612) Workstation Motherboard Review
summary: This review examines the Supermicro X10DAX workstation motherboard, highlighting its Hyper-Speed overclocking features and support for multi-GPU configurations. The article details its specifications, layout, BIOS, and performance through various benchmarks, comparing it to the X10DAi model. It concludes that the X10DAX offers excellent performance and stability for enthusiasts and professional applications requiring high-end computing power.

title: Nvidia CEO addresses GeForce GTX 970 scandal in a letter to customers
summary: Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang wrote an open letter to customers addressing the GeForce GTX 970 memory controversy. He admitted the company failed to clearly communicate the segmented memory architecture, but maintained the card is still a "4GB" adapter. Huang apologized for the communication lapse and promised improvements for future product launches, though no compensation was offered to affected customers.

title: Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang Apologizes For 'Miscommunication' On GTX 970 Specs
summary: Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang apologized for a "miscommunication" regarding the specifications of the GeForce GTX 970 graphics card. The issue stemmed from the advertised 4GB memory, which was actually 3.5GB with a segmented 512MB of lower bandwidth. Huang attributed the problem to a failure in communication between Nvidia's engineering and marketing divisions and promised clearer feature details in the future.

title: NVIDIA Launches Its First Living-Room Entertainment Device
summary: NVIDIA introduced SHIELD, the world's first Android TV console, which delivers 4K entertainment and high-performance gaming to the home. Powered by the Tegra X1 processor, SHIELD offers access to numerous Android titles and AAA games through the GRID game-streaming service, aiming to transform digital entertainment. The device, priced at $199 with a controller, launched in May 2015 and received support from leading game developers.

title: Nvidia GeForce Titan X 12GB: What you need to know and expect
summary: Nvidia unexpectedly unveiled its high-performing GeForce GTX Titan X graphics card at the Game Developers Conference. This new card will feature 12GB of GDDR5 memory and the "Big Maxwell" GM200 graphics processor, aiming for significantly higher performance than the GeForce GTX 980. Despite its consumer gaming focus and lack of native double precision FP64 compute capabilities, it is expected to be a very expensive card, possibly retailing around $1349.

title: NVIDIA CEO Talks Titan X, Next-Gen Pascal, Deep Learning And Elon Musk At GTC 2015
summary: NVIDIA CEO Jen-Hsun Huang's GTC 2015 keynote covered deep learning, the GeForce GTX Titan X's launch at $999, and upcoming Pascal GPU architecture features like 3D-stacked memory and NVLink. The presentation also highlighted the Digits DevBox and included a discussion with Tesla CEO Elon Musk on autonomous vehicles and AI.

title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang declare self-driving cars “solved”
summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk and Nvidia CEO Jen-Hsun Huang discussed the future of self-driving cars at the 2015 GPU Technology Conference. Musk stated that autonomous driving is a "solved problem" and addressed the challenges in urban environments and the lengthy transition period for the automotive industry. Huang highlighted Nvidia's new technologies like Titan X and Drive PX, emphasizing the car as a "software computer on wheels."

title: Elon Musk Predicts Human Drivers Will Be Outlawed in the Future
summary: Elon Musk predicted that human drivers could be outlawed in the future due to the safety risks posed by human-operated vehicles, referring to cars as "two-ton death machines." He later clarified on Twitter that Tesla is strongly in favor of people being allowed to drive their cars. The article also discusses Tesla's Autopilot system and a concept Musk proposed to accelerate the deployment of autonomous cars by having them operate passively in the background to gather data.

title: SK Hynix demos HBM2 memory ICs, opens way for 32GB graphics cards
summary: SK Hynix demonstrated HBM2 memory ICs at CeBIT, which are expected to significantly boost memory bandwidth and capacity for next-generation graphics cards. HBM2 chips will enable graphics adapters with up to 32GB of onboard memory and 1TB/s peak bandwidth, with production planned for early 2016. AMD's upcoming Radeon R9 390X is expected to be among the first graphics cards to utilize HBM memory.

title: AMD still has not started to use 20nm process tech
summary: Advanced Micro Devices has not yet begun using 20nm fabrication technology, despite prior announcements to use it for select products like "Skybridge" processors and a low-cost Xbox One SoC. This delay means that any 20nm chips from AMD will not be available until the second half of the year, and upcoming mid-2015 graphics processing units will continue to use the 28nm process. There are also rumors that TSMC's 20nm process may be unsuitable for complex custom designs.

title: Nvidia's futuristic Santa Clara campus is back on
summary: Nvidia and its general contractor, Devcon, are moving forward with plans to construct the first of two new headquarters buildings in Santa Clara. This development comes after months of cost reduction efforts, with the design of the new campus retaining its distinctive triangular shape. The new campus will be in addition to Nvidia's current headquarters, which it leases from the Sobrato Organization.

title: Gigabyte unveils two GeForce GTX 960 graphics cards for mini-ITX PCs
summary: Gigabyte has introduced two new GeForce GTX 960 graphics cards, the GV-N960IX-2GD and GV-N960IXOC-2GD, specifically designed for small-form-factor mini-ITX systems. These cards feature Nvidia's GM206 GPU with 2GB GDDR5 memory and a compact 17cm length, making them suitable for all computer chassis. They offer competitive performance for gamers with SFF builds, with varying clock speeds between the two models and advanced cooling systems.

title: Tegra K1 SoC
summary: The NVIDIA Tegra K1 SoC will remain available until January 2024, with L4T sustaining releases continuing as needed. The Jetson TK1 Developer Kit has reached End-of-Life and is no longer available, with NVIDIA JetPack 3.1 being its final supported JetPack version. The Tegra K1 series processors integrate a power-optimized Kepler GPU, enabling advanced features like OpenGL 4.4 and CUDA on mobile and embedded devices, supporting applications from autonomous robotics to medical imaging.

title: Nvidia To Sell Its Icera Business & Exit The Mobile Chip Market
summary: Nvidia has announced its decision to wind down its Icera modem operations by Q2 fiscal 2016 and is open to selling the business, effectively exiting the mobile baseband market due to intense competition against companies like Qualcomm and Samsung. The company's strategy is now to focus on high-growth opportunities in gaming, automotive, and cloud computing applications, where its visual computing expertise is highly valued. This move comes after Nvidia's 2011 acquisition of Icera failed to significantly increase its share in the mobile baseband market, with the Tegra 4i chip not living up to expectations.

title: Nvidia’s Tegra X1-based Shield game console certified in S. Korea
summary: Nvidia's second-generation Shield game console, powered by its Tegra X1 application processor, has been certified in South Korea. This certification by the RRA suggests Nvidia's intentions to sell the product commercially, despite the previous Shield Portable not achieving widespread popularity. The new device, identified as P2523, will feature the powerful Tegra X1 SoC, which includes ARM Cortex-A57 and A53 cores, and Maxwell graphics.

title: Nvidia’s GeForce GTX Titan X gets more affordable in the U.K.
summary: The Nvidia GeForce GTX Titan X graphics card, previously priced at £899 in the U.K., is now available for a discounted price of £799 through retailers like Overclockers UK, Palit, and Zotac for a limited time. This price reduction comes as initial demand for the flagship card has subsided, and new competitors like the GeForce GTX 980 Ti and AMD’s Radeon Fury are entering the market. The article notes that despite the brand, all Titan X cards are manufactured under Nvidia's supervision, ensuring consistent quality.

title: AMD reveals specs of AMD Radeon R9 300-series: Old GPUs get new life
summary: AMD has unveiled its new Radeon R9 and R7 300-series graphics cards, which are primarily re-badges of existing GPUs with minor clock-speed boosts and new software features like VSR and FRTC. While they offer performance improvements over their predecessors and are better positioned against competitors like Nvidia, the new cards are not expected to deliver breakthrough performance and some models are considered overpriced. The flagship R9 Fury-series will exist separately.

title: MapD: Massive Throughput Database Queries with LLVM on GPUs
summary: MapD leverages NVIDIA GPUs to achieve significantly better performance on data analytics tasks, utilizing the massive parallelism and memory bandwidth of GPUs like the NVIDIA Tesla K80 Accelerator. The company employs LLVM-based Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation to transform query plans into architecture-independent intermediate code for efficient execution on various architectures, including NVIDIA GPUs and x86-64 CPUs. This approach results in substantial performance gains, with queries using filter and aggregate operations reaching over 80% of available bandwidth and achieving 40-50x speedups on multi-GPU systems compared to high-end dual-socket CPU systems.

title: iShares MSCI All Country Asia ex Japan ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NASDAQ:AAXJ)
summary: This article provides detailed information about the iShares MSCI All Country Asia ex Japan ETF (AAXJ), including its current price, key statistics, holdings, and news. It outlines the ETF's objective to track the MSCI All Country Asia ex Japan Index and lists significant institutional shareholders and top sector holdings. The piece also includes an overview of its expenses and frequently asked questions about the fund.

title: Microsoft might be interested in buying AMD, according to source
summary: A source familiar with the matter indicates that Microsoft Corp. may acquire Advanced Micro Devices to revive its chip design operations. Microsoft has substantial cash reserves compared to AMD's market capitalization, making an acquisition relatively easy given AMD's current valuation is significantly lower than their purchase of ATI Technologies in 2006. Such a move could lead to considerable savings for Microsoft on components for its Xbox One and other hardware devices.

title: Nvidia CEO touts ‘ping-pong’ strategy for Tegra system-on-chips
summary: Nvidia's CEO, Jen-Hsun Huang, has introduced a new "ping-pong" strategy for its Tegra system-on-chips, aiming for more predictable two-year evolutionary cycles similar to Intel's former "tick-tock" model. This strategy will allow for alternating updates to CPU architecture and fabrication technology while retaining graphical architecture, or vice versa, ensuring significant performance improvements every 1.5 to 2 years. The goal is to provide greater predictability for customers and software developers, particularly in the growing automotive industry, though the alignment of CPU and GPU development cycles within Nvidia remains a challenge.

title: Chip designer Arm slips after disappointing Taiwan Semiconductor results
summary: Chip designer Arm's stock fell 4p to £10.41 after Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) reported disappointing revenue figures for June, which were down 14.5% compared to May and 0.6% year-over-year. Liberum reiterated a 'sell' recommendation on Arm, highlighting the close correlation between TSMC's performance and Arm's due to most Arm-technology chips being manufactured by TSMC.

title: TSMC cuts prices of 20nm and 28nm chips by 10%
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) has reduced prices for its 20nm and 28nm chip production by 10% earlier this quarter due to decreased orders and declining utilization rates. This price cut aims to boost capacity utilization above 80% and could benefit companies like AMD, Nvidia, Qualcomm, and MediaTek by lowering their manufacturing costs. The move comes as demand for these chips has softened, particularly in the mobile sector, with Apple significantly reducing its 20nm orders in anticipation of new technologies.

title: AMD Reports Loss of $0.23 Per Share, Graphics and OEM Business in Decline – Quarterly Earnings Report Q2 2015
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) reported a loss of $181 million, or $0.23 per share, for Q2 2015, marking a significant decline from the previous year. The company's revenue fell to $942 million, an 8% sequential decrease and 34% year-over-year, largely due to a decrease in APU sales and struggles in its computing and graphics segments, particularly impacting its OEM business. Despite the challenges, AMD anticipates a more positive trend in the next quarter driven by new GPU sales from Fiji chips and an updated OEM lineup.

title: 15-Way AMD/NVIDIA Graphics Card Comparison For 4K Linux Gaming Review
summary: This article provides a 15-way comparison of AMD and NVIDIA graphics cards for 4K Linux gaming performance, featuring the latest drivers and including the NVIDIA GeForce GTX 980 Ti. It details the extensive hardware setup and software configurations used for benchmarking and highlights the disproportionate availability of review samples from NVIDIA compared to AMD. The review also previews upcoming comparisons focusing on OpenCL compute numbers and power consumption.

title: Nvidia reportedly slashes price of GeForce GTX 750 Ti
summary: Nvidia is reportedly cutting the price of its GeForce GTX 750 Ti graphics cards by €15-€20 in preparation for the launch of its new GeForce GTX 950-series products. This price adjustment aims to make the GTX 750 Ti more competitive against AMD's Radeon R7 360 and clear inventory for the upcoming GM206-based solutions. The new GeForce GTX 950 series is expected to offer higher performance than the GTX 750 Ti.

title: EVGA GTX 980 Ti K|NGP|N hits 2.1GHz/8.4GHz with LN2, sets new records
summary: Vince "K|NGP|N" Lucido, a top overclocker, achieved new world records for single-GPU setups by overclocking an EVGA GeForce GTX 980 Ti K|NGP|N graphics card to 2100MHz/8400MHz (GPU/memory) using liquid nitrogen. This accomplishment pushed Nvidia's GM200-310 GPU to an unprecedented frequency, demonstrating the extreme overclocking potential of EVGA's specialized hardware. The heavily overclocked system set new highs in 3DMark Fire Strike, Fire Strike Extreme, and Fire Strike Ultra benchmarks.

title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2016
summary: NVIDIA reported revenue of $1.153 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2016, a 5 percent increase year-over-year, driven by strong growth in gaming and automotive sectors. Despite a GAAP earnings per diluted share of $0.05 due to charges, non-GAAP earnings per diluted share rose 13 percent to $0.34. The company returned $452 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases and provided an optimistic outlook for the third quarter.

title: Pixar Animation Studios Licenses NVIDIA Technology for Accelerating Feature Film Production
summary: Pixar Animation Studios has licensed a suite of NVIDIA technologies, including quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) rendering methods, to accelerate the production of its feature films and short content. This multi-year agreement aims to make rendering more efficient, especially with GPU acceleration, and enhance rendering functionality to significantly reduce rendering times. NVIDIA will also contribute ray-tracing technology to Pixar's OpenSubdiv Project for more precise rendering of complex subdivision surfaces.

title: Nvidia’s GeForce GTX 950 Ti is still in development
summary: Nvidia is reportedly still developing the GeForce GTX 950 Ti, a new graphics card based on the GM206 processor. This card is intended to bridge the performance gap between the existing GTX 950 and GTX 960 models, potentially offering 896 stream processors and 4GB of GDDR5 memory in premium versions. While its release timeline is uncertain, the GTX 950 Ti could appeal to budget gamers and HTPC enthusiasts due to its features like DirectX 12 support and H.265 encoding/decoding.

title: TSMC obtains orders from AMD and Nvidia for 16nm FinFET chips
summary: Despite being behind Samsung Foundry with its first-generation FinFET technology, TSMC has secured orders from major customers, including AMD and Nvidia, for its 16nm FinFET manufacturing process. AMD plans to use TSMC for its next-generation Radeon GPUs ("Greenland") and GlobalFoundries for 14nm microprocessors, while Nvidia will continue its partnership with TSMC for its GP100 graphics chip based on the Pascal architecture, even after adding Samsung Foundry as a partner. TSMC's 16nm FinFET client list also includes Apple, Avago, Broadcom, HiSilicon Technologies, LG Electronics, MediaTek, and Xilinx.

title: Supermicro 1028GQ-TRT Quad GPU 1U SuperServer Review
summary: This article reviews the Supermicro 1028GQ-TRT Quad GPU 1U SuperServer, highlighting its key features such as support for four GPUs and two Xeon E5 V3 processors, dense compute capabilities, and cooling design. It details the hardware, cooling mechanisms, remote management, test configuration with AMD FirePro S9150 GPUs, and performance benchmarks including AIDA64, Linux-Bench, and power consumption tests. The review concludes that the server offers significant computational power in a compact form factor, suitable for high-density compute or VDI applications.

title: Nvidia announces ‘deep learning’ R&D centre in Singapore
summary: Nvidia has announced the establishment of the Nvidia Technology Centre Asia Pacific in Singapore, focusing on deep learning research and development. The company plans to invest over S$20 million (US$14.2 million) in the center over three years and will partner with Singaporean government agencies and institutions to drive innovation and talent development. The center will develop solutions for Singapore's Smart Nation initiative, intelligent video analytics, and large-scale data analytics.

title: NVIDIA GRID 2.0 Launches With Broad Industry Support
summary: NVIDIA launched GRID 2.0, its cloud graphics technology, with significant industry backing from companies like VMware, Citrix, HP, and Dell. This new version offers doubled user density and application performance, blade server support, and Linux compatibility, enabling enterprises to virtualize graphics-intensive applications more efficiently and securely. Several Fortune 500 companies are already trialing or successfully implementing the technology, reporting benefits in productivity, IT efficiency, and security.

title: Asus unveils 34” curved ultra-wide 100Hz IPS LCD with Nvidia G-Sync
summary: Asustek Computer has revealed the Asus ROG Swift PG348Q, a 34-inch curved ultra-wide IPS display featuring a 100Hz refresh rate and Nvidia G-Sync technology, designed for gamers. This monitor is the first of its kind to combine these high-end specifications. While pricing and exact release dates were not disclosed, it is expected to be a premium product costing over £1000/$1300/€1300.

title: Asustek demos world’s first IPS gaming display with 165Hz refresh rate
summary: Asustek Computer demonstrated the industry's first gaming monitor with a 165Hz refresh rate, the ROG Swift PG279Q, featuring Nvidia's G-Sync technology and an IPS panel. This prototype is designed for professional gamers, offering a unique combination of high refresh rate and good color reproduction. While details like pricing and availability were not disclosed, it is expected to be a premium product despite some technical questions regarding its 165Hz capability with DisplayPort 1.2.

title: AMD: We are actively promoting HBM and do not collect royalties
summary: AMD has stated it is actively promoting High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and is not collecting royalties, despite co-developing the technology. This comes amid rumors that Nvidia was delaying HBM adoption due to AMD's royalty demands, which AMD denies, emphasizing that HBM IP is part of a JEDEC standard requiring licensing under reasonable terms or without compensation. Nvidia's "Pascal" architecture will support HBM2, with GPUs expected in 2016, though mass availability might be slow due to production schedules from SK Hynix and Samsung.

title: MSI teams up with Corsair for hybrid-cooled graphics cards
summary: MSI announced it is nearing the launch of graphics cards with hybrid cooling solutions, with one of the first adapters being an Nvidia GeForce GTX 980 Ti. This development follows a trend set by AMD and other manufacturers toward hybrid and liquid cooling systems. MSI and Corsair have collaborated on a GTX 980 Ti Watercooled prototype aimed at overclockers, promising higher clock-rates than Nvidia's reference design.

title: EVGA GeForce GTX 980 Ti FTW: Extreme performance, lower cost
summary: EVGA introduces a new graphics card, the GeForce GTX 980 Ti FTW, which offers nearly 20% higher clock-rates than reference boards at a more moderate price point. This model aims to balance cost, performance, and overclocking potential for enthusiasts, featuring a custom PCB and the ACX 2.0+ cooling system. The FTW is priced at $689 in the U.S., making it a slightly more affordable option compared to EVGA's Classified series.

title: Supermicro 4028GR-TR 4U 8-Way GPU SuperServer Review
summary: This article reviews the Supermicro 4028GR-TR 4U 8-Way GPU SuperServer, highlighting its key features such as support for up to 8 GPUs/Xeon Phis, dual Xeon E5 processors, and 24 hot-swap drive bays. The review details its internal layout, cooling system, power consumption, and thermal performance under stress tests using 8x AMD FirePro S9150 GPUs, concluding that it's a well-designed system for high-performance workloads, particularly in a new colocation facility.

title: How Did Marvell Technology Compare to Its Peers?
summary: Marvell Technology underperformed its peers based on gross profit margin and price-to-book value (PBV) ratio in 2Q16. ETFs investing in Marvell also outperformed the company based on price movement and PBV ratio. The article compares Marvell's financial metrics and stock performance against competitors like STMicroelectronics, NVIDIA, Freescale Semiconductors, and Texas Instruments, as well as relevant semiconductor ETFs.

title: Nvidia changes roadmap: ‘Volta’ is now due in 2018
summary: Nvidia has updated its GPU architecture roadmap, indicating that "Pascal" GPUs will launch in 2016, followed by "Volta" graphics processors in 2018. This change suggests a slight delay for "Volta," which was previously anticipated in 2017. The article also discusses Nvidia's new strategy of releasing its largest GPU chip first with the "Pascal" generation, a departure from its historical approach.

title: Nvidia readies new dual-chip GeForce GTX flagship graphics card
summary: Nvidia is developing a new dual-chip GeForce GTX flagship graphics card featuring two GM200 GPUs, aiming for extreme performance against AMD's Radeon R9 Fury X2. This card, likely part of the GeForce GTX Titan range, is expected to boast up to 6144 stream processors and a very high price, potentially taking advantage of the absence of direct competition if AMD delays its dual-chip offering. The memory configuration, either 12GB or 24GB, is still unclear, with 24GB presenting challenges for power consumption and cooling.

title: MSI rolls-out limited edition GeForce GTX 980 Ti with copper cooler
summary: MSI has introduced a limited edition GeForce GTX 980 Ti Gaming 6G Golden graphics card featuring a unique design, three operational modes, and an all-copper cooling system. This card is factory overclocked and expected to outperform Nvidia's GeForce GTX Titan X. It will be showcased at Madrid Games Week and released in the coming weeks.

title: Samsung and Qualcomm didn't infringe Nvidia patents says ITC
summary: The U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) has ruled that Samsung and Qualcomm did not infringe on two Nvidia graphics patents, although one Nvidia patent was infringed but deemed invalid. This decision comes over a year after Nvidia initiated a lawsuit against the chipmaking rivals. Nvidia plans to review the ruling in February 2016, while Samsung has also filed a patent lawsuit against Nvidia.

title: Rackspace Forges First “Barreleye” OpenPower Servers
summary: Rackspace has moved its "Barreleye" OpenPower server, based on IBM's Power8 architecture, from design to physical hardware. This initiative aims to create an open hardware and software stack, similar to the Open Compute Project, providing Rackspace and other hyperscalers with custom-fit hardware to enhance competitiveness. The Barreleye system, designed as a "megaserver," offers superior compute, memory, and I/O bandwidth compared to standard Xeon servers and is being developed with partners like IBM, Mellanox, Samsung, Avago Technologies, and PMC Sierra, with Ingrasys Technology as the system integrator.

title: Microsoft Surface Book’s Nvidia GPU is decent, but it’s no gaming laptop
summary: Microsoft's Surface Book features a dedicated Nvidia GPU, which new reports suggest is equivalent to the mid-range GeForce 940M. While this makes the Surface Book capable for average laptop use and some gaming at lower settings, it is not competitive with dedicated gaming laptops due to its focus on portability and battery life. The Surface Book does, however, hold an advantage over the Macbook Pro in gaming thanks to its Windows operating system and a broader game library.

title: Nvidia’s CEO, Jen-Hsun Huang, Receives a Brand New Tesla Model X P90D – Congratulates Elon Musk and Nvidia’s Team
summary: Nvidia's CEO, Jen-Hsun Huang, received a new Tesla Model X P90D, likely as a recognition of Nvidia's crucial role as a supplier for Tesla Motors, powering its digital cockpit system with Tegra chips. This event highlights the strong partnership between Nvidia and Tesla, particularly as Tesla moves towards autonomous vehicles, with Nvidia's Drive PX and Drive CX chips expected to play an increasingly significant role. Huang publicly congratulated Elon Musk and both the Tesla and Nvidia teams, emphasizing the increasing importance of Nvidia's technology in autonomous driving.

title: Intel Z170 Motherboard Roundup > Supermicro C7Z170-SQ
summary: This article reviews the Supermicro C7Z170-SQ motherboard, highlighting its features and comparing it to other Z170 boards. It notes Supermicro's push into the consumer market from its server background, discussing aspects like PCIe slot configuration, storage options, audio, networking, and the BIOS user experience. The review points out some limitations in its design for multi-GPU setups and its basic consumer features compared to competitors.

title: Isha Salian Author Page
summary: This page features Isha Salian, a writer on NVIDIA's corporate communications team, specializing in deep learning, science, and healthcare. It showcases a collection of articles she has authored for the NVIDIA Blog, covering topics like AI in healthcare, NVIDIA's partnership with OpenAI, and various NVIDIA Research breakthroughs in AI and graphics.
